Issues.Title: JIT `ɵɵngDeclareComponent` defaults pre-v22 library components to OnPush; the AOT linker keeps them on Default (`hasOnPushByDefault` version rule is missing in `convertDeclareComponentFacadeToMetadata`)
Issues.Body: ### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler ### Is this a regression? Yes ### Description A library compiled with Angular < 22 in partial compilation mode (`ɵɵngDeclareComponent({ version: "20.3.x", ... })`) whose component omits `changeDetection` is handled differently by the two consumers of that declaration in an Angular 22 application: - **AOT (partial linker)** keeps it on `Default`/`Eager`: `packages/compiler-cli/linker/src/file_linker/partial_linkers/partial_component_linker_1.ts` computes `hasOnPushByDefault = major >= 22 || version === PLACEHOLDER_VERSION` and only then falls back to `OnPush`. That is correct: a component written for v20 was always checked and may assign state inside subscriptions or callbacks without `markForCheck()`. - **JIT (`ɵɵngDeclareComponent` → `ɵcompilerFacade.compileComponentDeclaration`)** ignores the declared version: `packages/compiler/src/jit_compiler_facade.ts`, `convertDeclareComponentFacadeToMetadata`, uses `changeDetection: decl.changeDetection ?? ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`. The same v20 component becomes `OnPush` and silently stops re-rendering. JIT is what Storybook (`@storybook/angular`), Jest (`jest-preset-angular`), Vitest without the AOT plugin, `TestBed` and `ng serve --aot=false` use, so a library that works in the built application breaks in every one of those. We hit it with Kendo UI for Angular 25 (compiled with Angular 20.3): its internal `TreeViewGroupComponent` assigns nodes inside a subscription and rendered an empty tree in Storybook, while the AOT build was fine. This is the declare-path counterpart of #70262. That issue is about the JIT *decorator* path (`@Component` metadata → `Eager`) diverging from AOT (`OnPush`) for the app's own components. Here the JIT *declare* path (library partial declarations) diverges from the linker in the opposite direction: it applies the v22 default to declarations that predate v22. The two paths disagree with AOT in different ways, so fixing #70262 alone does not fix this. Expected: the JIT declare path applies the same rule as the linker, i.e. `OnPush` only when `decl.version` is >= 22 (or the placeholder version), `Eager` otherwise. Workaround we use in Storybook/Vitest (must run before any library declaration is evaluated): ```ts import '@angular/compiler'; import { ChangeDetectionStrategy } from '@angular/core'; const facade = (globalThis as any).ng?.ɵcompilerFacade; const original = facade.compileComponentDeclaration.bind(facade); facade.compileComponentDeclaration = (env: unknown, url: string, decl: any) => { const major = Number.parseInt(String(decl.version ?? '0').split('.')[0], 10); const patched = decl.changeDetection == null && major > 0 && major < 22 ? { ...decl, changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager } : decl; return original(env, url, patched); }; ``` ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug https://github.com/diegohoyos/angular-jit-onpush-repro ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true No exception. The component compiled through ɵɵngDeclareComponent gets ɵcmp.onPush === true and its view is never refreshed after the subscription assigns new state. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.2.0 Angular : 22.2.0 Node.js : 22.23.2 Package Manager : npm 12.0.2 Operating System : win32 x64 ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐ │ Package │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │ ├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ @angular/build │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/cli │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/common │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/compiler │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/compiler-cli │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/core │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ rxjs │ 7.8.2 │ 7.8.2 │ │ typescript │ 6.0.3 │ 6.0.3 │ │ zone.js │ 0.16.3 │ 0.16.3 │ └───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘ The library (legacy-lib) was compiled with @angular/compiler-cli 20.3.33 / typescript 5.8.3, compilationMode: "partial". ``` ### Anything else? - `packages/compiler-cli/linker/.../partial_component_linker_1.ts`: `const hasOnPushByDefault = major >= 22 || version === PLACEHOLDER_VERSION;` then `changeDetection: metaObj.has('changeDetection') ? ... : hasOnPushByDefault ? OnPush : Eager`. - `packages/compiler/src/jit_compiler_facade.ts`, `convertDeclareComponentFacadeToMetadata`: `changeDetection: decl.changeDetection ?? ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` with no look at `decl.version`. - Reproduces on 22.0.x through 22.2.0.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "JIT `ɵɵngDeclareComponent` defaults pre-v22 library components to OnPush; the AOT linker keeps them on Default (`hasOnPushByDefault` version rule is missing in `convertDeclareComponentFacadeToMetadata`)" (#71107)

Issues.Title: fix(router): unsubscribe from route data when outlet deactivates
Issues.Body:
When `RouterOutlet.deactivate()` is called, the outlet destroys the active component but previously did not unsubscribe from route data. This left the route data subscription and resource binding effects (`outletEffects`) active in the input binder until either the next component was activated on that outlet or the outlet itself was destroyed via `ngOnDestroy`.

This commit updates `deactivate()` to call `inputBinder?.unsubscribeFromRouteData(this)`, eagerly tearing down the route-data subscription and resource binding effects at destroy time.

The "Render phases" section says that a phase is specified by passing an object with a `phase` property to `afterRender` or `afterNextRender`, but the example below uses `afterRenderEffect` with one callback for each phase.

Neither the `afterRender` name nor the `phase` option matches the current API. `afterRender` was renamed to `afterEveryRender` in #60999, and the phase option was replaced by the per-phase callback object in #55648.

The chart example above also calls `this.canvas().nativeElement()` even though `nativeElement` is a property of `ElementRef`, not a method.

## What is the new behavior?

The description now matches the current `afterRenderEffect` API by explaining that phases are specified with an object containing a callback for each phase.

The chart example also uses `this.canvas().nativeElement`.

Issues.Title: fix(router): fall back when serializing protocol-relative URLs
Issues.Body:
Avoid throwing when DefaultUrlSerializer encounters a UrlTree that would serialize to a protocol-relative URL. Warn in development mode and serialize the tree with a root-relative path instead while preserving query parameters and fragments.

Additionally, account for WHATWG URL normalization (e.g. dot segments and backslashes collapsing into protocol-relative paths such as `/.//` or `/..//`).

Fixes #69700
Fixes #71076

Issues.Title: fix(router): fall back when serializing protocol-relative URLs
Issues.Body:
Avoid throwing when DefaultUrlSerializer encounters a UrlTree that would serialize to a protocol-relative URL. The exception surfaced existing test data and mistaken command construction as a breaking change after #69874.

Warn in development mode and serialize the tree as "/" instead. Keep the browser-facing URL root-relative without changing command or route-recognition semantics.

The original fix had to be reverted after a regression surfaced in g3: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/69874#issuecomment-5321181936

This uses the less disruptive fallback proposed in the follow-up discussion: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/69874#issuecomment-5331535428

Fixes #69700

Requires TGP

Issues.Title: Private members used only in the template are reported as unused (TS6133)
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler-cli, language-service ### Is this a regression? No ### Description Since #70188 (22.2.0), a template can read `private` members of its component. TypeScript doesn't see those reads though, so a `private` member that is only used in the template is still reported as unused (TS6133). ```ts import {Component, signal} from '@angular/core'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', template: `

{{ privateTitle() }}

{{ protectedTitle() }}

`, }) export class App { private readonly privateTitle = signal('private member'); protected readonly protectedTitle = signal('protected member'); } ``` With `"noUnusedLocals": true` in `tsconfig.json`, `ng build` fails: ``` ✘ [ERROR] TS6133: 'privateTitle' is declared but its value is never read. [plugin angular-compiler] src/app.ts:12:19: 12 │ private readonly privateTitle = signal('private member'); ╵ ~~~~~~~~~~~~ ``` `ng serve` fails the same way on startup. Without `noUnusedLocals` the build passes, but the editor still greys out `privateTitle` and offers the "Remove unused declaration for: 'privateTitle'" quick fix, which breaks the template when applied. The Angular language service forwards TypeScript's suggestion diagnostics as is, so having the extension installed doesn't change this. `protectedTitle` isn't reported in either case, since TypeScript doesn't track unused `protected` members. I'd expect a `private` member read by the component's own template to count as used, both in the build and in the editor. Whatever the fix, private members that are genuinely unused should still be reported, since that's what `noUnusedLocals` is for. This came up in https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/70514#issuecomment-5813840954, opening a separate issue so it can be tracked on its own. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug The component above, with `"noUnusedLocals": true` in `tsconfig.json`. ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true TS6133: 'privateTitle' is declared but its value is never read. ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true Angular CLI : 22.2.0 Angular : 22.2.0 Node.js : 24.21.0 Package Manager : npm 11.19.0 Operating System : darwin arm64 ┌───────────────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┐ │ Package │ Installed Version │ Requested Version │ ├───────────────────────────┼───────────────────┼───────────────────┤ │ @angular/build │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/cli │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/common │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/compiler │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/compiler-cli │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/core │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ @angular/platform-browser │ 22.2.0 │ 22.2.0 │ │ rxjs │ 7.8.2 │ ~7.8.0 │ │ typescript │ 6.0.3 │ ~6.0.2 │ └───────────────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┘ ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): preserve nested workspace path for git worktree cache
Issues.Body:
When an Angular workspace is located in a subdirectory of a Git repository rather than at the repository root, resolving the shared cache path in a Git worktree previously walked up to the worktree root to find the `.git` file and then resolved the cache path directly against the main repository root (`dirname(commonGitDir)`). This discarded the relative path between the worktree root and the workspace root.

`getCacheBasePath` now computes the relative path from the worktree root to `workspaceRoot` and resolves the target workspace directory in the main repository. If the corresponding workspace directory exists in the main repository, the cache path is resolved relative to it; otherwise, it falls back to the worktree-local workspace root to avoid creating untracked directories in the main repository. Additionally, the directory traversal now stops at the nearest `.git` boundary.

Fixes #34215

Issues.Title: perf(@angular/build): avoid sharding intermediate files under worker surplus in i18n inliner
Issues.Body:
When the number of uncached files in an inlining window meets or exceeds
the worker pool concurrency, the thread pool already has sufficient
file-level parallelism to keep all workers fully utilized.

Previously, all intermediate files (files between 100 KB and 70% of the
maximum file size) were sharded into batches of half their locales
regardless of the total file count. In applications with many chunks,
this doubled the number of worker tasks and forced multiple worker threads
to independently parse the same JavaScript file and decode the same source
map.

Intermediate files are now processed with all window locales in a single
batch whenever the file count is greater than or equal to the worker thread
count. This halves the task count for intermediate chunks, eliminates
redundant AST and sourcemap parsing across threads, and reduces IPC and
scheduling overhead.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "perf(@angular/build): avoid sharding intermediate files under worker surplus in i18n inliner" (#34219)

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): add fast path for untranslated messages in i18n inliner worker
Issues.Body:
When inlining a locale without translations (such as the source locale or when a translation dictionary is undefined), calls to translateMessage() previously invoked ɵtranslate() with an empty dictionary. This caused @angular/localize to throw a MissingTranslationError for every single $localize message site in the application, catching it to retrieve the original message parts from the parsed message.

Throwing and catching thousands of Error instances incurs significant V8 stack trace capturing and exception handling overhead.

translateMessage() now provides an early fast path when translations is undefined: it directly calls ɵparseMessage(messageParts, substitutions) to parse and strip metadata/placeholder markers without throwing or catching exceptions.

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #34131

Library builds force `importHelpers`, and bare specifiers are externalized, so an emitted bundle can carry a live `import ... from 'tslib'`. `generatePackageManifests` only passes `dependencies` through from the source manifest and never creates it, so a library that does not declare tslib itself produces a package with no `dependencies` field at all. A tslib the library already declares, in `dependencies` or in `peerDependencies`, is left exactly as it is. When `@angular/compiler` cannot be resolved nothing is added and the output keeps the dependencies the library declared.

The range is resolved in `normalizeOptions`, where the builder already reads the filesystem, so `generatePackageManifests` stays pure and the four new cases are plain unit tests.

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

ng-packagr also moves a `peerDependencies.tslib` into `dependencies` with a warning. That is not done here: it is a separate behaviour change and this function has no logger.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular-devkit/build-angular): do not mark standalone expression statements as pure
Issues.Body:
Top-level call and new expressions that appear directly as expression statements are executed solely for their side effects, such as class property initialization, static blocks, and helper calls.

When targeting browsers requiring class static block or property lowering (e.g., Chrome < 94), Babel's preset-env lowers self-referencing static properties into zero-argument IIFEs (and static blocks into _staticBlock() calls). Because pure-toplevel-functions previously only skipped IIFEs if they had arguments, zero-argument IIFE statements were marked as pure. Downstream minifiers (such as esbuild) then eliminated these standalone pure statements as dead code, dropping essential class members like Injector.ɵprov and causing NG0201 at bootstrap.

This change ensures that call and new expressions that are directly expression statements are never annotated as pure, avoiding accidental elimination of side-effecting statements without requiring hardcoded whitelists of helper function names.

Fixes #34017

Issues.Title: [22.2.x]perf(@angular/build): process batch locales sequentially in i18n inliner worker
Issues.Body:
Executing batch locales concurrently via Promise.all within a single
worker thread provided no concurrency benefit because inlining operations
(MagicString transformations and source map decoding/remapping) are
predominantly synchronous and CPU-bound on Node's single-threaded event loop.

Holding concurrent MagicString instances, intermediate AST slices, and
decoded source map mappings simultaneously inflated peak worker heap and RSS
(especially for smaller chunks where up to 8 locales are processed in a single
batch).

Switching to sequential iteration allows intermediate transformation and
mapping structures to be garbage-collected between locales, reducing peak RSS
and slightly improving throughput due to reduced GC pressure.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): merge component stylesheet metafiles in a stable order
Issues.Body:
**Build output is non-deterministic: two builds of identical sources can write different stats files. Merging the component stylesheet metafiles in a stable order fixes it.**

## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-commit-message-guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #34209

`outputs[<file>].inputs` in the stats file changes between builds of the same sources. The cause is one loop in `build.onEnd`: the compiler plugin merges each component stylesheet's metafile into the main metafile in the order the stylesheets finished bundling, and when two stylesheets produce the same output file, the last one merged owns the entry. Every emitted file is byte-identical; only the metadata moves.

## What is the new behavior?

The entries are sorted by key before merging, so the merged metafile is the same on every build.

The new spec builds two components in different directories with identical stylesheets, builds twice, and asserts the shared output is attributed to the same input both times.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [x] No

## Other information

Measured on 22.1.9 with the reproduction at https://github.com/sdjayna/angular-metafile-merge-order-repro (60 components, 12 identical-stylesheet pairs, 4 identical-image pairs): without the change 5 of 5 build pairs differed, in 7 to 10 of 54 `outputs` entries; with it, 0 of 3 differed and the stats file was byte-identical. The same loop is on `main` today. The sort runs once per build over one entry per stylesheet, so its cost does not register against the bundling.

Issues.Title: stats.json is non-deterministic when two component stylesheets produce the same output file
Issues.Body:
## Command

build

## Is this a regression?

No. Present since the esbuild-based builder merged stylesheet metafiles this way.

## Description

**Build output is non-deterministic: two production builds of identical sources write different `stats.json` files, while every emitted JS, CSS and media file is byte-identical.**

The cause is one loop. In `packages/angular/build/src/tools/esbuild/angular/compiler-plugin.ts`, `build.onEnd` merges each component stylesheet's esbuild metafile into the main metafile with `Object.assign` while iterating `additionalResults.values()`. That map fills as each stylesheet finishes bundling, so its order changes from build to build. When two stylesheets produce the same output file name, two components with the same file name and byte-identical SCSS, or two identical images referenced from different stylesheets, each metafile claims the output with its own `inputs`, and the last one merged wins. `outputs[<file>].inputs` then names one source on one build and the other on the next.

`statsJson: true` makes it visible, but the merged metafile is the one esbuild hands to every `onEnd` callback, so any consumer of `result.metafile` sees the same flip.

## Minimal Reproduction

Repository: https://github.com/sdjayna/angular-metafile-merge-order-repro

```sh
npm ci
scripts/repro.sh          # builds twice, compares stats.json, hashes dist/repro/browser
scripts/repro-loop.sh 5   # repeats the pair 5 times, counts flips
```

The app is a fresh `ng new repro --style=scss` with `statsJson: true` and `outputHashing: "all"` in the production configuration, plus 60 generated standalone components: 12 pairs share a file name and byte-identical SCSS across `src/app/a` and `src/app/b`, and 4 pairs reference byte-identical PNG files from two asset folders.

Expected: two production builds of identical sources write identical `stats.json`.

Actual: every build pair differed in 7 to 10 of the 54 `outputs` entries (5 of 5 pairs). Emitted files under `dist/repro/browser` had identical SHA-256 hashes in every pair.

```
build 1: 4 s
build 2: 2 s
emitted files under dist/repro/browser: identical (8 files)
stats.json: differs
outputs: 54
outputs whose inputs differ: 9
  dup-0-4P5FWS4E.css
    run1: src/app/a/dup-0/dup-0.scss
    run2: src/app/b/dup-0/dup-0.scss
  dup-10-FB2SWP2Q.css
    run1: src/app/b/dup-10/dup-10.scss
    run2: src/app/a/dup-10/dup-10.scss

    run1: angular:css-resource:src/app/a/img/pic-0.png
    run2: angular:css-resource:src/app/b/img/pic-0.png
```

Sorting `additionalResults` by key before the merge removes it: with that one-line change applied to `node_modules/@angular/build`, 0 of 3 pairs differed and `stats.json` was byte-identical. Reverting it brought the flip back. PR to follow.

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/ssr): prevent open redirect via protocol-relative pathname
Issues.Body:
The `Location` header for a server-side navigation was built by joining the `PlatformLocation` pathname with the search and hash. A pathname may start with `//`, which as a `Location` value is a protocol-relative URL to another origin. The router serializes `/.;/(//example.com)` to `/.//example.com`, dot-segment removal leaves `//example.com`, and a single unauthenticated `GET` returned `302 Location: //example.com`. Any route with a parameter in the first segment and a wildcard child is affected, with no redirect logic in the application.

Collapse the leading slashes of the pathname before using it as a location, and normalize the same way in `createRedirectResponse()`, which also prefixes a slash so the value cannot resolve anywhere but the current origin.

The collapse consumes tab, line feed and carriage return too: the WHATWG URL parser removes them before parsing, so a client reads `/\t/example.com` as `//example.com`. Tab is a legal header value character and reaches the wire, and prefixing a slash would otherwise turn a leading tab, which the header layer trims, into an inner one that it does not.
 
Fixes angular/angular#71076

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): resolve unit-test include patterns from the project root
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated

## PR Type

- [x] Bugfix

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #33467

Schema says `include` is relative to project root. Code resolves it from source root. So for a library with secondary entry point next to `src` nothing reaches it - `my-sub-package/**/*.spec.ts`, `./my-sub-package/**/*.spec.ts`, `my-sub-package/my-sub.spec.ts`, `projects/my-lib/my-sub-package/**/*.spec.ts` all find zero files and run still says success. Happens with no config too, `ng generate library` writes no `include`.

## What is the new behavior?

Pattern that matched nothing under source root gets retried from project root. Pattern that already matched is not retried, so `**/*.spec.ts` stays where it is and does not start picking up specs outside `src`. Project rooted at workspace root is never retried, that would search every project.

Checked on generated workspace with library, secondary entry point and an `e2e/` spec. Four spellings above fixed plus reporter's `["**/*.spec.ts", "my-sub-package/**/*.spec.ts"]`. Six spellings that work today return same files. `e2e/` spec not picked up before or after.

Cost is globbing per pattern instead of batching, needed to tell unmatched from matched. On library with 302 specs medians are 451ms before and 447ms after, spread between rounds is wider than that.

`builders/karma/find-tests.ts` untouched, it calls through without new argument so karma keeps current behavior.

Three of five new cases fail without the change. Other two pin what must not move.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): avoid loading localize tools and babel in i18n inliner worker
Issues.Body:
Previously, `i18n-inliner-worker.ts` dynamically loaded `@angular/localize/tools` to invoke its `translate()` function and `Diagnostics` class. Importing `@angular/localize/tools` eagerly pulls in `@babel/core`, `@angular/compiler-cli`, and `@angular/compiler`, consuming ~180 ms of CPU latency and ~32 MB of heap per worker thread upon first translation.

Since the inliner only performs string translation replacements using AST locations already discovered via OXC, the full Babel transformation and compiler tooling bundle is unnecessary.

This updates `i18n-inliner-worker.ts` to directly import low-level runtime functions (`ɵtranslate`, `ɵisMissingTranslationError`, `ɵmakeTemplateObject`) from `@angular/localize` and manage diagnostics via a direct message array. This completely avoids loading `@angular/localize/tools` and its heavy transitive dependencies.

Issues.Title: unit-test builder (Vitest, 22.2.0 OXC linker): ReferenceError on class referenced by name before its own declaration in a partially-compiled npm library
Issues.Body:
### Command

test

### Is this a regression?

Not sure — this may be a regression introduced by the linker rewrite in 22.2.0 ("migrate Angular Linker to oxc-parser and magic-string"), since I have not tested this with 22.1.x.

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

When running `ng test` with the `@angular/build:unit-test` builder (Vitest runner) on Angular CLI / @angular/build 22.2.0, several test files fail to load at all (0 tests reported, whole suite crashes) with:

ReferenceError: Cannot access 'CascadeSelect' before initialization
at CascadeSelectSub.<static_initializer> node_modules/@openng/src/cascadeselect/cascadeselect.ts:131:30


I traced this to the actual shipped file (the path above is a sourcemap reference, not a real file on disk):
`node_modules/@openng/optimus-ui/fesm2022/openng-optimus-ui-cascadeselect.mjs`

In that file, `CascadeSelectSub` is declared at line 176, and its static Ivy partial declaration at line 274 includes:

```js
static ɵfac = i0.ɵɵngDeclareFactory({ ..., type: CascadeSelectSub, deps: [{ token: CascadeSelect }], target: i0.ɵɵFactoryTarget.Component });
```

`CascadeSelect` (the referenced class) is not declared until line 452, further down in the same file. Since this is emitted as a literal `class` declaration (temporal dead zone applies), referencing the identifier `CascadeSelect` before its declaration executes throws a `ReferenceError` — unless the Angular linker processes this partial-compilation output (`ɵɵngDeclareFactory`, `ɵɵngDeclareComponent`) into a fully-linked form first, which is presumably not order-sensitive.

This same package builds and tests fine under the classic Karma + `@angular-devkit/build-angular` pipeline, which suggests the linker is applied correctly there but not (or not correctly) for this specific cross-class-reference pattern under the `unit-test` builder in 22.2.0.



### Minimal Reproduction

I don't have an isolated reproduction yet, but you've provided the full trace and the exact line of the affected packet.

### Exception or Error

```text
ReferenceError: Cannot access 'CascadeSelect' before initialization
❯ CascadeSelectSub.<static_initializer> node_modules/@openng/src/cascadeselect/cascadeselect.ts:131:30
❯ node_modules/@openng/src/cascadeselect/cascadeselect.ts:131:39

(Note: the path shown is from the package's sourcemap; the real file evaluated is `node_modules/@openng/optimus-ui/fesm2022/openng-optimus-ui-cascadeselect.mjs`.)
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI: 22.2.0
@angular/build: 22.2.0
Vitest: 5.0.2
Node: v24.21.0
OS: Windows
```

### Anything else relevant?

- The affected npm package is `@openng/optimus-ui` (latest version at time of reporting).
- The broken class is `CascadeSelect` / `CascadeSelectSub`, distributed in Ivy partial-compilation format (`ɵɵngDeclareComponent`, `ɵɵngDeclareFactory`).
- `CascadeSelectSub` is declared earlier in the file than `CascadeSelect`, and its factory's `deps` array references `CascadeSelect` by identifier without going through `forwardRef`.
- This surfaced right after upgrading to 22.2.0, which per the changelog migrated the Angular Linker to oxc-parser/magic-string and included several linker-related fixes in the same release (syntax corruption, parenthesized expressions, source mapping). This may be an edge case not yet covered by the new OXC-based linker implementation.
- Affects every test file whose import graph pulls in this component (via a shared header/footer module), causing the whole suite (not just one test) to fail to load — reported as "(0 test)" by Vitest.

Issues.Title: Server builder assets can overwrite the generated main.js entry point
Issues.Body:
### Command

`build`, `run`

### Is this a regression?

No. The server builder has copied configured assets after Webpack output since the `assets` option was released in 15.1.0.

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

No response.

### Description

`@angular-devkit/build-angular:server` copies configured assets after Webpack emits the server program, without checking whether an asset destination is already a generated file.

With a recursive asset tree copied to output `.`, an asset named `main.js` silently replaces the generated server entry point. The build reports success, and normal `node dist/server/main.js` startup executes the asset instead of the generated application bundle.

I reproduced this with an asset-only dependency update. Version 1.0.0 contains only `assets/data.json`; version 1.0.1 adds only `assets/main.js`. Neither version declares `scripts`, `main`, `exports`, `imports`, or `bin`, installation uses `--ignore-scripts`, and the application never imports the package.

Expected: the build should reject an asset/generated-output collision, or keep generated output authoritative.

Actual: the build succeeds and the final `dist/server/main.js` is byte-for-byte identical to the dependency asset. Starting it executes dependency-controlled code as the deployed server process.

### Minimal Reproduction

Repository: https://github.com/BlueIridium-Security/angular-server-asset-entry-collision-repro

```sh
git clone https://github.com/BlueIridium-Security/angular-server-asset-entry-collision-repro.git
cd angular-server-asset-entry-collision-repro
./scripts/validate.sh
```

The validator runs clean → attack → restored-clean → restored-attack. Across two fresh-container runs, clean 1.0.0 always emitted and started the same genuine 782,472-byte bundle with no marker; attack 1.0.1 always emitted the exact 192-byte package asset and executed its marker. Runtime networking is disabled, and the script fails on any control mismatch.

### Exception or Error

No exception is reported. The builder reports successful bundle generation and asset copying.

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI: 22.2.0
@angular-devkit/build-angular: 22.2.0
Angular: 22.2.0
Node: 24.21.0
npm: 11.19.0
OS: Linux arm64 container (node:24.21.0-bookworm-slim)
```

### Anything else relevant?

The builder is deprecated but remains shipped. The default server `assets` list is empty, and exploitation requires an opt-in recursive root-output rule plus an accepted package update, build, deployment, and startup. I therefore assess this as High rather than Critical.

Current source shows the [server builder calling `copyAssets()` after successful Webpack output](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/e023a8e1ac36203fa5d5343b7920b0c6033212ff/packages/angular_devkit/build_angular/src/builders/server/index.ts#L80-L126), while [`copyAssets()` writes each destination without checking generated outputs](https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/blob/e023a8e1ac36203fa5d5343b7920b0c6033212ff/packages/angular_devkit/build_angular/src/utils/copy-assets.ts#L41-L60).

This is distinct from #19157 and #16670, which discuss precedence between two configured asset inputs rather than a post-Webpack asset replacing the executable generated entry point.

Should the server builder reject configured asset destinations that collide with generated output files?

Issues.Title: refactor(@angular/build): lazy load sourcemap remapping in js transform worker
Issues.Body:
Previously, `@ampproject/remapping` was statically imported at the top level of `javascript-transformer-worker.ts`, eagerly pulling in 5 packages (`@ampproject/remapping` and 4 sub-dependencies) upon worker initialization.

In standard Angular CLI configurations (`ng build` and `ng serve`), vendor sourcemaps are disabled by default (`thirdPartySourcemaps = false`), causing `useInputSourcemap` to evaluate to false for all transformed `node_modules` files. As a result, sourcemap remapping is never executed in typical builds.

Issues.Title: perf(@angular/build): cache transformed configuration in TypeScript compilation
Issues.Body:
When `rootFiles` are explicitly provided (e.g. in library builds), re-parsing `tsconfig.json` and traversing the project directory structure via `readConfiguration` on every incremental watch rebuild is redundant and adds measurable overhead (~200-350ms on large libraries).

This change caches the `TransformedConfiguration` in `TypeScriptCompilation` when explicit `rootFiles` are provided and invalidates the cache only when a `.json` configuration file changes.

See: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/71034

Issues.Title: docs: convert component sidenav to signals
Issues.Body:
Replaces the `async` pipe usages in `ComponentSidenav` and `ComponentNav` with signals. The breakpoints are converted using `toSignal`, which also allows the templates to be simplified.

`ComponentNav` was injecting `ActivatedRoute` to read the `section` param, because it isn't a routed component. Now `ComponentSidenav` receives the `section` param as an input through the router's component input binding and passes it down to `ComponentNav`, which loads the section's items through a `resource`. Adds a test that navigates through the routes and checks that the navigation lists the items of the section.

Also fixes the sidenav closing logic which was checking the `isScreenSmall` observable instead of its value.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs: convert component sidenav to signals" (#33910)

Issues.Title: refactor(material/sort): inject AriaDescriber as required
Issues.Body: `MatSortHeader` was injecting `AriaDescriber` as optional and guarding every call with optional chaining. `AriaDescriber` is always available since it's automatically provided, and `MatTooltip` and `MatBadge` already inject it as required, so we can drop the optional flag and the null checks.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(material/sort): inject AriaDescriber as required" (#33899)

Issues.Title: docs: convert version picker to signals
Issues.Body: Replaces the `async` pipe in the version picker with an `httpResource`. If the versions can't be loaded, the picker doesn't list any versions, like before. Also adds tests for the version picker, which didn't have any.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs: convert version picker to signals" (#33909)

Issues.Title: refactor(multiple): remove workaround for blur during change detection
Issues.Body:
`MatCheckbox` and `MatSlideToggle` were deferring marking their form control as touched to a microtask, because a focused element that gets disabled fires `blur` during change detection which used to throw a changed-after-checked error (angular/angular#17793). This is no longer the case since views that are marked for check during change detection are refreshed within the same pass and the form status classes are computed.

These changes remove the workaround and add tests that disable a focused control with Zone.js-based change detection. The existing zoneless tests already cover the same case.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(multiple): remove workaround for blur during change detection" (#33907)

Issues.Title: refactor(cdk/drag-drop): warn when the list changes while dragging
Issues.Body:
Prior to this commit, it was impossible to catch the source of this problem. While an item is dragged, its element is moved out of the list and into the body. The framework still uses that element as the anchor for the views around it. So a re-render of the list during a drag can throw, and the error comes from the renderer, which says nothing about the code that changed the list.

Steps that lead to the warning:
1) The user starts dragging an item in the list.
2) The app changes the list while the drag is still going on. For example an
   upload finishes and adds one more image.
3) The framework renders the new item and inserts it next to the dragged
   element, which is not in the list anymore. Angular then throws NG05106.

The warning is printed only in dev mode and only once per drag sequence. It names the real cause at the moment it happens, so nobody has to guess it from the renderer's error later.

The observer is created outside of the Angular zone, so it never triggers a change detection cycle.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(cdk/drag-drop): warn when the list changes while dragging" (#33908)

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/menu): clear pending menu aim timeout on destroy
Issues.Body:
When the user moves towards an open submenu and stops on a sibling item, `TargetMenuAim` delays toggling the sibling's menu using a timeout. The timeout wasn't being cleared on destroy which meant that if the menu was destroyed while it was pending, the sibling's menu would still be opened afterwards.

These changes clear the timeout on destroy and remove the delay that the tests had to wait for after each test.

Issues.Title: test(cdk/drag-drop): switch custom preview fixture to control flow
Issues.Body: The custom preview test fixture was using `*ngIf` to work around a framework issue where a directive on an `ng-template` at the root of a control flow block was instantiated twice. The issue is no longer reproducible so we can switch to `@if` and drop the `NgIf` import.

Issues.Title: fix(material/form-field): update outlined label offset when direction changes
Issues.Body:
In #31643 we added a workaround that copied `Directionality.valueSignal` into a property through an `effect`, because reading the signal inside an `afterRenderEffect` was causing a memory leak (angular/angular#62980). As a side effect, the `afterRenderEffect` that positions the label of an outlined form field with a prefix no longer depended on the direction, so the label offset wasn't recalculated if the direction changed at runtime.

The framework issue was fixed in angular/angular#63001 so these changes remove the workaround and read the direction directly again.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(material/form-field): update outlined label offset when direction changes" (#33896)

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/overlay): allow users to opt into closing on any URL change
Issues.Body:
Expands the `disposeOnNavigation` config option to allow users to opt into closing on any URL change, not just popstate.

Fixes #33665.

Issues.Title: docs: resolve guide and doc items in the router
Issues.Body:
`GuideViewer` and `ComponentViewer` looked up their item from the route params themselves, and called `router.navigate` when nothing matched. That meant the component was created and rendered before the redirect, and the redirect started a second navigation.

This moves the lookup into route resolvers. When an item is missing, the resolver returns a `RedirectCommand`, so the router redirects as part of the same navigation, before the component is created. When it's found, the item reaches the component as an input through `withComponentInputBinding()`.

Changes:
- Add `guideResolver` on the `guide/:id` route. It resolves the guide or redirects to `/guides`.

Issues.Title: docs: type the external redirect guard
Issues.Body:
`externalRedirect()` passed its guard to `canActivate` as an inline arrow function. `canActivate` accepts `CanActivateFn` as well as the deprecated class-based guards, typed as `ProviderToken<any>`. Any function also matches `ProviderToken<any>`, so TypeScript didn't check the inline guard against `CanActivateFn`. For example, a guard returning a number would still compile.

This declares the guard as a `CanActivateFn` before passing it to `canActivate`, so its return value is type checked. The behavior is unchanged. A comment explains why the type is needed, so it isn't inlined again later.

Issues.Title: docs: bind route params to component inputs
Issues.Body:
The routed pages in the docs app read their route params by subscribing to `ActivatedRoute` by hand. `ComponentViewer` combined its own params with its parent's to get both `:id` and `:section`, and `ComponentCategoryList` walked `pathFromRoot` and merged the params of every level to find `:section`.

This enables `withComponentInputBinding()` so that the router passes the route params to the routed components as inputs. Nested routes already receive their parent's params, because the router's params inheritance strategy defaults to `always`, so no further router config is needed.

Changes:
- `GuideViewer`: add an `id` input and derive the guide with `computed`. An `effect` sets the page title, or redirects to `/guides` if no guide matches the id.
- `ComponentViewer`: add `id` and `section` inputs and load the doc item from them with `toObservable` and `switchMap`, which still cancels a lookup when the params change before it finishes. The child pages keep reading `componentDocItem`, so they're unchanged.
- `ComponentCategoryList`: add a `section` input and turn the summary and items into signals, updating the template to read them. An `effect` sets the page title.
- Drop the `ActivatedRoute` injections, `combineLatest` and manual param merging from these components.

Tests:
- Rewrite the `GuideViewer` spec with `RouterTestingHarness` and a real route config, and cover the redirect for an unknown guide.
- Add specs for `ComponentViewer` and `ComponentCategoryList` whose routes match the app's nesting (`:section` > sidenav > page). They cover the params reaching the inputs, the page title, and the component being reused and updated when the params change.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "docs: bind route params to component inputs" (#33884)

Issues.Title: docs: cross-fade between pages with view transitions
Issues.Body:
Navigating between pages in the docs app swapped the content instantly. This enables the router's `withViewTransitions()`, so browsers that support the View Transitions API cross-fade from the old page to the new one. Other browsers keep the current behavior.

Changes:
- Add `withViewTransitions({skipInitialTransition: true})` to the router config. The first page load isn't animated, since there's no previous page to transition from.
- Add a global `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` rule that disables the view transition animations, so those users get an instant page swap.

Checked in Chrome against the dev server, comparing against a run with `document.startViewTransition` removed to get the behavior without transitions:
- Clicking a category card runs a 250ms cross-fade of the root.
- The first page load doesn't start a transition.
- Focus still moves to the new page's `focusOnNavigation` target.
- Navigating to another page with a `#fragment` still scrolls the target heading into view, at the same position as without transitions.
- With reduced motion, the transition starts but runs no animations.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "docs: cross-fade between pages with view transitions" (#33888)

Issues.Title: fix(cdk/drag-drop): avoid rendering pre-drop order in zoneless apps
Issues.Body:
When an item is dropped, the `DropListRef` resets the DOM to its pre-drag order and emits the `dropped` event. With zone.js change detection runs synchronously when the `NgZone` is exited so the new order is rendered before the browser paints. In zoneless apps change detection is scheduled asynchronously which allows the browser to paint the stale order in between, causing the dropped item to blink.

Fixes #33837.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "fix(cdk/drag-drop): avoid rendering pre-drop order in zoneless apps" (#33881)
